messages:
nina: Hey team — after installing the python SDK today I get ImportError on startup. Using Python 3.8 in a poetry venv.

nina: Error is `ImportError: cannot import name 'Literal' from 'typing_extensions'` when importing redwood.client.

nina: pip/poetry output looked normal, I did `poetry add redwood-inference` then `poetry run python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)"` and it fails.

matt (support): thanks for reporting, can you paste `python -c "import sys, typing_extensions; print(typing_extensions.__version__, sys.version)"` and `poetry show redwood-inference`?

nina: sure — output: ```

nina: 3.7.4 3.8.10 (default, Jun  4 2023, 10:00:00)

nina: Name: redwood-inference

nina: Version: 0.6.1

nina: Description: Redwood inference SDK
```

matt (support): OK that typing_extensions is oldish (3.7.4). Newer SDKs sometimes require typing_extensions >= 4.x for backported typing features on py3.8. Poetry should have pulled a compatible version but lockfiles or other deps can pin an older one.

matt (support): Can you run `poetry run pip check` and `poetry run pip list --format=columns | grep typing-extensions`?

nina: `pip check` shows no conflicts. `pip list` shows `typing-extensions 3.7.4`

matt (support): That explains it. The SDK imports `Literal` from typing_extensions on older Pythons; older typing_extensions doesn't export that symbol. Quick fix: `poetry add --dev "typing-extensions>=4.0.0"` (or without --dev if you need it at runtime), then `poetry lock --no-update` or `poetry update typing-extensions`.

nina: ran `poetry add typing-extensions@^4.0.0` and now `poetry run python -c "import redwood; print('ok')"` succeeds, thanks. One question — how did poetry allow the older typing-extensions to remain?

devex_julia: common reasons: another dependency in your lockfile pinned typing-extensions <4, or the lockfile was generated earlier and you installed from it. Poetry won't automatically bump transitive deps unless you update them. Also pyproject extras/groups and platform markers can cause different resolution.

devex_julia: longterm we recommend pinning a minimum typing-extensions in your pyproject for Python<3.9: e.g. `dependencies = ["typing-extensions>=4.0.0 ; python_version < \"3.9\""]` so that any fresh lock includes the right version.

matt (support): we'll note this in the troubleshooting KB. For now: summary steps we gave — check typing-extensions version, upgrade it in the environment, or recreate lock with `poetry lock -n && poetry install` to pull compatible transitive deps.

nina: awesome, worked for me. adding note: `pip install redwood-inference` on same machine without venv also had typing-extensions 3.7.4 system package, so be careful with system site packages.

pkg-bot: Automated note: Logged as support ticket #6342, label: sdk-install.

matt (support): closing thread — reopen if you hit another import after upgrading. :thumbsup:
